title: Hearing the great southwest bands, 1926-37, to learn musicians
summary: He explains he developed his ear for musicians by listening to Dallas, Oklahoma City, Tulsa and Kansas City bands like Gene Coy, Buster Smith and Booker Pitman.

bands.name: Gene Coy and His Black Aces

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Ernie, you started out very young as a bandleader and I wonder how at that young age and all down through the years you were able to be so astute and sharp at selecting musicians and so forth?

what, I would say from 1926 to 1937 I really became very much involved in music, and at that time I had the chance to hear some of the greatest. Believe it or not, if you come to think about it, some of the greatest musicians that we have in America, came from the Dallas, Oklahoma City, Tulsa and Kansas City area, and even Little Rock. That's where the Southern Serenaders hailed from.
Along about that time, Chauncy Downs from Kansas City would come in with his band ; Paul Banks--have you ever heard of Gene Cory and the Black Aces?
Incidentally, that's the band Junior Raglin left here with Gene Cory in 1935.

Another star in there was Booker Pitman, and I think he finally went across in Europe. Ben Webster, Joe Keyes, Jack Washington, and you see, during that time, (inaudible), Buster Smith out of Dallas and George and Julia

Lee band, Jap Allen, and so you see, whenever they played a dance--I never was participating in a jam session, but some of my men was always there, and I would be there looking to see what was happening, and you could get to see what was going on and make your choice and just see what was going on.
